wu: Color Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher holds up a flashcard (e.g., red), and the first student runs to the board, draws a red object, and says 'It is a big red ball'. The team with the correct drawing and sentence gets a point.
wuAlt: Color Bingo: Students have bingo cards with color words. Teacher calls out 'Find something blue in the classroom', and students mark the word if they see blue.
Color Chain: One student says 'I see something red', the next says 'I see something red and blue', and so on, building the chain.
pres: Teacher uses a story about a Moroccan market (souk) with colorful items. Flashcards show a 'big yellow lemon', 'small green mint', and 'long red pepper'. Model sentences: 'What color is it? It is a big yellow lemon'. Check understanding by asking 'What color is the mint?'
presAlt: Realia Show: Teacher brings real fruits (lemon, apple, banana) and asks 'What color is it?' Students answer 'It is a yellow banana'.
Color Song: Sing 'I See Something Blue' with gestures, then pause and ask 'What color is the pen?'
prac: Team Quiz Show: Two teams compete to describe pictures. For example, Team A gets a picture of a 'small black cat' and must say 'It is a small black cat'. Teacher gives sentence starters: 'It is a...'.
pracAlt: Picture Match: Students get two sets of cards—color words and adjective+color phrases (e.g., 'big red'). They match them.
Describe and Compare: In pairs, Student A describes a picture (e.g., 'It is a big blue car'), Student B finds the matching picture from two options.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a picture: 'It is a big green ball and a small yellow ball'. Students draw and compare. Checks if they can spot adjective order.
re: Color Jump: Students stand in a circle. Teacher calls out 'Jump to red!', and students jump to the red flashcard. After the break, this reactivates movement and color words.
prod: Comic Strip Project: In groups, students draw a 2-frame comic strip with two colorful objects (e.g., a big red kite and a small blue kite). They add speech bubbles: 'What color is it?' and 'It is a big red kite'.
rw: Read and Match: Students read short sentences like 'It is a long green snake' and match them to the correct picture. Then they write their own 2-sentence description: 'It is a big yellow sun. It is hot.'
st: Story: 'The Rainbow Over the Atlas Mountains' (a short story about colors in nature). End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students run to board to draw/color objects when teacher calls a color
Teams describe pictures to earn points
Match color words to adjective+color phrases
Teacher describes, students draw to check listening
Groups draw and write speech bubbles about colors
diff: Fast finishers: Add more details to their comic strip (e.g., 'It is a big, shiny red kite').
Support: Use word banks with color words and adjectives (big, small, long, short).
hw: Draw a comic strip with 2 frames about colors and add speech bubbles (e.g., 'What color is the flag? It is red and green').
Write 3 sentences about colors in your room (e.g., 'My bed is blue. My pillow is white.')
Find 5 colorful objects at home and write their colors (e.g., 'The door is brown. The carpet is red.')
tip: Use local context like the Moroccan flag (red and green) to make colors relevant. For the American Space, connect to US holidays like Independence Day (red, white, blue) to build cultural bridges.
